Duration::eq¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Series Duration::eq(const Duration& other) const;
Series Duration::operator==(const Duration& other) const;  // eq(other)

What It Does¶

Compares two Duration values elementwise by their underlying elapsed-nanosecond magnitude for equality, broadcasting under ordinary N-D rules, and returns a Series of booleans — one comparison result per broadcasted position.

Note

Series[bool], not a scalar bool This is the same design Timeline’s eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge use, and the opposite of Timeline’s own operator==/operator</etc. (which return a plain scalar bool, documented on TimelineBase). Duration’s operators are all wired to the Series-returning methods, with no scalar-bool sibling.

Parameters¶

other (const Duration&)

The duration to compare against. Broadcasts against self.

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series at the broadcasted shape, one comparison result per position.

Examples¶

Example 1. 90 minutes equals 1 hour is false.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
std::cout << pluss::print_series(one_hour.eq(ninety_min));

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=false

1 hour == 90 minutes is false (60 min != 90 min).

Notes¶

  • Comparisons are purely by elapsed magnitude — there is no notion of “direction” beyond sign; a negative Duration (see abs/sign) compares as less than a positive one, same as ordinary signed-number comparison.

  • operator== is documented sugar for eq — nothing is computed differently between the two spellings.

See Also¶

  • ne: the negation of this comparison.

  • lt, le, gt, ge: the ordering comparisons.

  • abs: magnitude and sign, relevant when comparing durations that may be negative.
